A named entity recognition (NER) model fine-tuned for the **automatic de-identification of clinical records** in Spanish. It detects and labels personally identifiable information (PII) in clinical text using BIO tagging scheme.

## Model description

This model was fine-tuned from [`PlanTL-GOB-ES/roberta-base-biomedical-clinical-es`](https://huggingface.co/PlanTL-GOB-ES/roberta-base-biomedical-clinical-es), a RoBERTa language model pre-trained on biomedical and clinical texts in Spanish.

Fine-tuning was performed on **real clinical records from maternal patients** at the Clínica Universitaria Bolivariana (Medellín, Colombia), making this a clinical de-identification model trained on free-text real word data in the colombian context.

The model classifies tokens using the **BIO** (Beginning – Inside – Outside) scheme for the following entity categories:

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| `B-NAME` | Beginning of a person's name |
| `I-NAME` | Inside/continuation of a person's name |
| `B-PROFESSION` | Beginning of a profession or occupation |
| `I-PROFESSION` | Inside/continuation of a profession or occupation |
| `B-LOCATION` | Beginning of a geographic location |
| `I-LOCATION` | Inside/continuation of a geographic location |
| `O` | Token outside any entity |

## How to use

```python
from transformers import pipeline

deid = pipeline(
    "token-classification",
    model="LabBiomedica/roberta-base-biomedical-clinical-es-finetuned-deid",
    aggregation_strategy="simple"
)

text = "La paciente María López, residente en Medellín, fue atendida por el Dr. Ramírez, médico internista."
result = deid(text)
print(result)
```

# RoBERTa Medical Triage Classifier

## Model Description

This repository contains a fully fine-tuned RoBERTa sequence classification model. Full fine-tuning updates the transformer encoder and the classification head.

The model receives a short English symptom description and predicts one of the following triage-oriented labels:

- `self_monitor`
- `consult_gp`
- `urgent`

This model was developed as part of the **SortMed** academic project, a medical pre-triage assistant prototype built for a bachelor's thesis by **Cristian Untaru** at the **West University of Timișoara, Faculty of Informatics**.

The model is intended for research and educational use. It is not a diagnostic system and is not a certified medical device.

## Intended Use

This model is intended to be used in an academic medical pre-triage prototype for:

- classifying English symptom descriptions into broad urgency categories;
- comparing transformer-based models for medical text classification;
- evaluating full fine-tuning against parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods;
- supporting experimental NLP research in symptom-based medical pre-triage.

Example input:

```text
I have chest pain, shortness of breath, and I feel dizzy.
```

Example output:

```text
urgent
```

## Out-of-Scope Use

This model must not be used as:

- a replacement for professional medical advice;
- a diagnostic system;
- an emergency decision-making tool;
- a certified clinical triage system;
- a standalone healthcare product;
- a tool for non-English medical text without additional validation.
